label: copy-phase input "e" fed back as 1st or 2nd original token
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, when the fed-back input is the letter e, at the first or second copy-input step (recall_idx 1 or 2, i.e. input e is original token 0 or 1). Magnitude depends strongly on position: when e is the first original token, fed back right after <DEL> (recall_idx 1), activation is strong (~0.8-1.0 of max, ~81% of activation mass, precision 1.0). When e is the second original token (recall_idx 2), activation is weak (~0.15-0.3 of max). Never fires during the original phase, on the delimiter, on e at later copy steps (recall_idx >= 3, only a handful of cases), or on other tokens (almost never).

issues: The claims hold up. Activity is zero in the original and delimiter phases. 100% of activation mass is on in_tok e. recall_idx 1 carries 0.809 of the mass and recall_idx 2 carries 0.191. recall_idx 3 has only 75 dev activations. On test, the recall_idx==1 predicate has precision 1.0 and F1 0.68. Full predicate on test: P 0.969, R 0.996, F1 0.983.

One small but systematic false-positive class depends on length. At recall_idx 2 the weak branch is length-gated. Precision is 0.158 at L=3 (457 predicted), 0.734 at L=4 (2425 predicted) and 1.0 at L>=5 (13841 predicted). Most of the ~1000 test false positives look like 'x e y <DEL> x *e*' with L=3 or 4. The explanation does not mention this.
The test misses (120 steps, 0.0% of mass) are scattered tiny activations (<0.05 of max), for example e at recall_idx 3. They are noise.
